paragraphs: A city museum that offers free admission one evening a week is often praised for widening access, and its attendance figures on those evenings are impressive. Yet attendance counts alone say little about whom the policy serves. A survey of free-evening visitors found that most came from households whose incomes were above the regional median, and many said they would have paid had no free evening been offered. The finding does not show that the policy is pointless, since a free evening can still introduce first-time visitors who later return on paying days, and the survey did not follow anyone long enough to say whether that happens. It does suggest, however, that if the aim is to reach people who rarely visit museums, free evenings may need to be combined with outreach in neighborhoods where the museum is little known, because lowering the price has plainly not reached those people on its own.
